title: The DFAM: Moog’s drum machine with no drums in it
intro: Moog Music released the DFAM, the Drummer From Another Mother, in 2017 as the second of its Mother-32 family of semi-modular desktop and Eurorack synths. Where a drum machine plays samples or fixed drum circuits, the DFAM is a whole analogue synth voice, two VCOs, noise, a Moog ladder filter and three decay envelopes, played by an 8-step sequencer with a pitch and a velocity knob per step. Its kicks, toms, snares and hats are all patches of one voice.

timeline.name: Moog modular
timeline.text: Robert Moog’s voltage-controlled modules, the ladder filter among them: the DFAM’s filter is that design.

timeline.name: Moog 960 Sequential Controller
timeline.text: Moog’s modular step sequencer gave each step a knob of its own, the way the DFAM’s PITCH and VELOCITY rows work.

timeline.name: Moog Mother-32
timeline.text: The first of the family: one VCO, a ladder filter and a 32-step sequencer, desktop or Eurorack, with a patchbay.

timeline.name: Moog DFAM
timeline.text: Two VCOs with hard sync and linear FM, white noise, an LP or HP ladder filter, three decay envelopes with voltage-controlled decay, an 8-step pitch and velocity sequencer clocked from 10 to 10,000 BPM, and a 24-point patchbay.

timeline.name: Moog Subharmonicon
timeline.text: The third of the family: subharmonic oscillators and polyrhythmic sequencers, made to clock and be clocked by the DFAM.

timeline.name: Behringer EDGE
timeline.text: Behringer’s recreation of the DFAM, adding pink noise, MIDI and USB clock, MIDI notes and a poly chain.

relatives.name: Moog Mother-32
relatives.text: The semi-modular it was made to sit beside: its assignable output, set to a clock, drives the DFAM’s ADV / CLOCK.

relatives.name: Moog Subharmonicon
relatives.text: A later member of the family, also in the app; its CLOCK OUT or TRIGGER can clock the DFAM.

relatives.name: Behringer EDGE
relatives.text: The recreation of the DFAM, also in the app.
